system: You are an expert front-end engineer. You write production-quality React and TypeScript for Next.js App Router projects.

messages.content:
Build the UI described below as a single page in an existing Next.js 16 project (App Router, React 19, strict TypeScript).

Stack: Once UI (`@once-ui-system/core` 2.1) is installed and its standard providers are mounted in the root layout; no documentation is available, so work from what you know.

Task: Chat UI — message list with avatars, streaming indicator, input bar with emoji picker, command palette hint.

Requirements:
- Write exactly one file, `app/page.tsx`, that default-exports the page. Put "use client" at the top if the page uses state, effects or event handlers.
- Do not create or change any other file. The root layout, global styles and the stack's standard providers already exist. You can read the project's existing files under `project/`.
- Use realistic placeholder content defined inline in the file (no lorem ipsum). Load nothing from the network: no external image, font or API URLs.
- The page must type-check under strict TypeScript, pass `next build`, and render without console errors.
- Make it responsive from phone to desktop, and accessible.
- Reply with the complete file in a single ```tsx code block and nothing else.

content.text: I'll start by inspecting the project's existing files to see how the providers and layout are set up.

content.thinking: I'll build the chat UI with trusted Once UI components (Flex, Column, Row, Text, Heading, Avatar, IconButton, Button, Kbd, Badge, Line, Tag), including a header, scrollable message log with reactions, a streaming typing indicator, an input bar with emoji popover, and a ⌘K command palette—using inline styles only for the dot animation.
